title: DRAM cell (1T1C)
summary: A DRAM cell stores 1 bit in a capacitor (1T1C: 1 transistor + 1 capacitor). The transistor (access) connects the capacitor to the bit line when the word line is asserted. Read: precharge bit line, assert word line, sense the charge sharing (destructive read). Write: drive bit line to desired value, assert word line (charges/discharges capacitor). Refresh required every ~64ms (capacitor leaks).

structure.meaning: Stores charge (1 = charged, 0 = discharged). Capacitance ~10-30 fF.
Connects capacitor to bit line when word line is asserted.
Precharge BL, assert WL, sense charge sharing. Capacitor is discharged (must rewrite).
Drive BL to desired value, assert WL. Capacitor charges/discharges.
Capacitor leaks; must read and rewrite every ~64ms (typically 8192 refreshes per 64ms).
Differential amplifier that senses the small voltage change on the bit line.

notes: 1T1C DRAM is the standard for main memory (dense: 1 transistor per bit).
DRAM is volatile (loses data when power is off).
DDR (Double Data Rate) transfers on both clock edges (2x bandwidth).
